s: A company runs a critical order-processing application in one AWS Region across three Availability Zones. The application uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon ElastiCache replication group, and an Amazon Aurora DB cluster with a replica in another Availability Zone. Leadership wants evidence that the application keeps processing orders if an entire Availability Zone loses power. The test must include the database failing over and new instances being unable to launch in the impaired Availability Zone, and it must end early if order throughput drops too far. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take? (Choose two.)
o: Create an experiment template from the AWS Fault Injection Service (AWS FIS) scenario library by using the AZ Availability: Power Interruption scenario. Target one Availability Zone and tag the resources the scenario should affect.
Create a CloudWatch alarm on an orders-per-minute business metric and add the alarm to the experiment template as a stop condition.
Stop the EC2 instances in one Availability Zone from the EC2 console and reboot the DB cluster writer with failover. Watch the application dashboards during the test.
Turn on Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal autoshift practice runs for the ALB and rely on the practice runs as the evidence.
Deploy a copy of the application in a second Region and configure Amazon Route 53 failover routing between the two Regions.

w.y: The AZ Availability: Power Interruption scenario in AWS FIS reproduces what a real AZ power loss looks like: instances stop, Auto Scaling cannot launch new instances in that zone, the Aurora cluster writer fails over, ElastiCache nodes in the zone are lost, subnet connectivity drops briefly, EBS I/O pauses during recovery and ARC zonal autoshift starts. A CloudWatch alarm on a business metric, attached as a stop condition, ends the experiment if orders fall too far.

o.A: Correct. The scenario includes the database failover and the pause on instance launches that the requirement asks for.
o.B: Correct. A stop condition on a business KPI is AWS's recommended way to keep a production experiment safe.
o.C: Stopping instances and rebooting with failover misses the key symptom: Auto Scaling can still launch replacements in the 'failed' zone, so the test proves less. It is also manual and not repeatable.
o.D: Practice runs shift traffic away from a zone to check that the rest has enough capacity. They do not fail the database or block launches, so they are only part of the evidence.
o.E: This is a Region-level DR design. The requirement is about surviving the loss of one Availability Zone inside the Region.
